mechanism_narrative: The transit series has broken its own range, dropping from -4.0 to -14.3 percent in one week. Because retail-and-recreation footfall in Greater London is dominated by transit-borne trips, this collapse in trip supply mechanically removes the customer base for discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days stays below its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -4.0 at t-1w to -14.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell from -1.9 to -11.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days equals or exceeds its last-28-day mean of -2.7 even though TRANSIT remains below -8.0 percent.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week jump in grocery-and-pharmacy mobility of +6.7 points to +9.3 percent signals precautionary stockpiling by households. Stockpiling consumes the same discretionary budget and calendar slots that would otherwise go to non-essential retail, so the retail-and-recreation series falls in the week immediately following the spike.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points week-on-week above its prior four-week mean
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 2.6 at t-1w to 9.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell to -11.4
failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM gains more than 5 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC one week later is higher than its pre-spike level in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: Transit and workplace mobility are falling together, producing a compounding loss of two independent retail trip generators: the commute-linked lunchtime and after-work market, and the transit interchange footfall around stations. The joint decline is multiplicative rather than additive, so RETAIL_REC declines further than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -14.3 and WORKPLACES at -4.4 are simultaneously negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers above -2.7 over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below zero, showing the joint effect is not multiplicative.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility rising to +3.0 while parks mobility falls to -5.1 describes a household lockdown-substitution pattern: out-of-home leisure is being relocated indoors rather than to non-essential venues. The combination suppresses discretionary retail trips more than the sum of the two individual moves.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 0.6 at t-1w to 3.0 at t-0w while PARKS fell from -0.6 to -5.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or above -2.7 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +2.0 and PARKS stays below -3.0.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week slide in parks mobility from +4.6 to -5.1 tracks the seasonal shift of outdoor leisure indoors. That reallocation moves household leisure spend from free outdoor activity into paid indoor venues counted in the retail-and-recreation series, lifting RETAIL_REC relative to a last-28-day window that ended at a seasonal trough.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined monotonically from +4.6 at t-3w to -5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below its last-28-day mean even as PARKS stays negative, showing no seasonal reallocation into indoor venues.

mechanism_narrative: When announced containment measures push RESIDENTIAL above +2.0 percent, the binding constraint on retail-and-recreation is the household stay-at-home instruction, not voluntary caution. Under that regime the retail series keeps declining for at least two weeks regardless of transit or park movements, because compliance is enforced rather than chosen.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +2.0 percent in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 3.0 at t-0w, its highest value in the four-week window, coinciding with RETAIL_REC at -11.4
regime_hint: newly announced containment measures within the trailing 7 days
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the following 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above +2.0 percent, indicating voluntary behaviour rather than enforced confinement.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC at -11.4 percent is a single-week outlier that pulls the last-28-day mean down to -2.7, an artificially depressed comparison base. Because the target compares the next 28 days against that depressed base, and the extreme week is unlikely to repeat at the same magnitude, RETAIL_REC mechanically prints higher over the coming four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC prints below -10.0 percent in the most recent week while its four-week mean is above -4.0
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 9.5 points week-on-week from -1.9 to -11.4, dragging the four-week mean to -2.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below -11.4 for the full next 28 days, so the coming four-week mean is still below -2.7.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility at +9.3 combined with transit at -14.3 shows trips are being consolidated into essential, single-purpose errands. When grocery and transit diverge this strongly, the marginal trip is an essential errand that bypasses retail-and-recreation sites entirely, so RETAIL_REC declines in the following week even if the grocery surge fades.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM minus TRANSIT exceeds 20 points in the most recent week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +9.3 and TRANSIT at -14.3 give a 23.6 point divergence at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC one week after a greater-than-20-point GROCERY_PHARM minus TRANSIT divergence is unchanged or higher than its level in the divergence week.
